name: cc-enslaver
description: A Claude Code plugin and LLM-agnostic rule pack that enforces systematic thinking, verified citations, and root-cause analysis — eliminating reactive, lazy AI behavior. v0.22 adds two write-time content detectors as rules 10 and 11. rule 10 (no non-essential hardcoding) denies an Edit/Write whose code inlines a credential: a secret-named identifier assigned a quoted literal, a PEM private-key header, an AWS access-key literal, or credentials embedded in a connection URL. rule 11 (no non-essential path dependency) denies code that bakes in a machine-specific user-home absolute path or a shell home variable, which breaks portability. Both mirror the rule-09 PreToolUse content-detector mechanism, share its adjacent why-comment escape hatch (how 'non-essential' is operationalized), exempt prose-doc and lockfile targets, and add no Stop layer. English remains the i18n skeleton and source of truth (rules/ + prompts/ at the root, default injection); Chinese is a first-class translation (rules/zh/ + prompts/zh/, via CC_ENSLAVER_LANG=zh), with drift CI-blocked by i18n_check.py + test_i18n_sync.py.
